text:
Quinn Hughes returns to Vancouver in a Wild sweater, on a 13-game point streak, for a team at the top of the NHL. Minnesota is 17-3-4 with 38 points, has won five straight by a combined 24-9, and has nine road wins in a row. The Canucks he left have 11 points, a 0.1% chance at the playoffs in our race, and a front office openly rebuilding: Max Sasson just went to the Rangers for a pick, and Elias Pettersson's name is all over the trade talk.

Our numbers are a little cooler on Minnesota than the standings. The Wild are plus 35 in goal difference on plus 18.1 expected, and most of that gap is Jesper Wallstedt, who is .925 with 19.1 goals saved above expected, perfect in November so far. That's not a fluke you dismiss, but it is the part most likely to come back toward earth. Kirill Kaprizov has a 13-game point streak too, Matt Boldy is one assist from 200 and has seven points in four games against Vancouver, and Brock Faber is back after a skull fracture, scoring in his first home game. Hughes' own run is mostly bounces: his shots are carrying less danger than usual.

For Vancouver the good news is Brock Boeser. He has a nine-game point streak and the city has started talking about him as a captain, a leader for whatever this rebuild becomes. Filip Hronek is one goal from 50 for his career. The rest is hard reading. The Canucks have 40% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) and allow 4.38 goals a game, and the Kraken just put 43 shots on them in a 5-1 loss.

Minnesota won the first meeting 4-2 on Oct 25, a game it deserved 94% of the time. The special-teams matchup is stark: the Wild's power play makes 0.87 expected goals a game and Vancouver's kill allows 0.95, with the Canucks taking 4.3 penalties a night.
headline: Quinn Hughes comes back to a rebuilding Vancouver
